title: Nonstandard Network Onramp Prioritization & Upgrade Runway for Private/VPC Deploys
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Define a lightweight, repeatable decision flow and prioritization rubric for Private/VPC/on-prem customer network requests that fall outside standard preflight paths (e.g., limited outbound, intermittent egress, custom airwall rules, legacy proxy appliances). Deliverables: 1) decision matrix for runway classification (fasttrack / scheduled / engineering-assist), 2) concrete staging patterns (transit-proxy adapter, ephemeral jump host, offline bundle strategy), 3) clear upgrade windows and rollback lanes for customers on restricted networks, 4) a templated intake form and SLA commitment text for sales/CS to set expectations.
updates: 2025-03-13: Kickoff meeting with Solutions Eng + Infra. Agreed to avoid laborious per-customer network diagrams at Triage; use a 4-question probe to classify network runway (egress ports, allowed domains, cert lifecycle, maintenance window cadence). Action: SE to draft probe questions (owner: Marisol Vega).

2025-03-14: Architecture review with Runtime Eng. Identified two compatible staging patterns: (A) transit-proxy adapter that sits in customer DMZ to broker traffic; (B) pre-signed bundle + airgap installer for fully offline installs. Runtime needs a slimmed bootstrap for airgap (estimate 5 points). Added dependency ENG-1842 for bootstrap work.

2025-03-15: Draft intake form created in Confluence and sample email template for CS (link in artifacts). Product to request legal language for SLA on patching windows for customers that decline remote agent install. (owner: Aisha).

2025-03-17: Prioritization rubric proposed: customer impact (revenue/tier) x effort (estimated infra eng days) x risk (data-sensitivity). For MVP, fasttrack allowed for customers with up to 3 blocked ports if they accept transit-proxy pattern. Feedback requested from GTM by 2025-03-20.

2025-03-18: Security review pre-check queued. Security raised cert rotation and key escrow questions for transit path; flagged security_review_required. Next step: schedule 30m with Security (owner: Liam).
notes: Avoids creating per-customer custom engineering projects for low-revenue requests by steering to one of three repeatable patterns. Will be reviewed with Sales leadership to align expectations and with Security to validate key management. If accepted, produce a CS-facing triage playbook and a one-page runbook for Solutions Eng.
next_steps: (1) SE to finalize probe questions and sample network capture template by 2025-03-20; (2) Runtime ENG to estimate bootstrap changes (follow up ENG-1842); (3) Schedule security sync; (4) Draft CS SLA language and email template; (5) Pilot rubric with 3 open customer requests.
